_how: a new patient, prediction only (no collapsed lung): copy to configs/<patient>.json, set patient, data_dir, output_dir and the file names in inputs, then: python main_predict.py --config configs/<patient>.json --collapse 50 [--params calibration/<rule>.json] [--frames 30] [--run pred50]. The first run builds the geometry (geometry, hilum, fem_setup); without --params, E comes from the built-in rule physics.E_Pa {rule: collapse}

inputs._comment: surfaces from 3D Slicer (data_dir), LPS: the inflated lung (lung_left.vtk or lung_right.vtk) and the three trees for the hilum. collapsed: null (prediction only)

fem_setup._comment: clamp: triangles within sphere radius x radius_factor of the anchor points. wall.surface: 'reference' (the inflated surface), a file, or null; grid_mm / smoothing_mm: the wall as a smooth field (solver.wall_update potential). regions: {levels: [...]} only for physics.perturbation regions

physics._comment: a parameter is a number (fixed) or {fit: true, init, bounds} (fitted by the fit step). gravity: position of the inflated CT and of the collapse (supine | prone | left_lateral | right_lateral | [x, y, z] LPS), null = no gravity. collapse: q0 (p/E) | p0_Pa | volume_ratio. perturbation (fit only): null | {gradient: [ap, si, ml]} | {regions: [K, ...]}
physics._ct_density: optional: "ct_density": <kg/m3 measured on the CT> to also report E and p0 at the patient's density
physics._collapse: volume_ratio = V_collapsed / V_inflated to reach: 0.5 = 50 % collapse (rule calibrated on 23-86 %)

solver._comment: core: torch | warp | getfem (validation); the rest are the core's options (eurelaps_lung/fem/solvers/nodal.py)
